text:
rachel: Quick async check-in — yesterday I finished the tinyq onboard smoke runs for llama3-tinyq. Found a small regression on the summarization prompt set: hallucination rate up ~4% vs baseline. I opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/412 to revert the prompt tweak and keep the old template for now. Can folks skim and approve if it looks safe?
sam: On it. I saw the same blip in reranking evals this morning. I suspect the quantization profile + new prompt tokenization interacts oddly. Will run a targeted eval.
eli: Do you have the exact eval command you used? I want to reproduce locally before reviewing the PR.
rachel: Repro command I ran on CI: ```
python eval.py --model llama3-tinyq --promptset summarization_v2 --split dev --batch 16 --quant-profile q4_0 --save results/tinyq_summarization.json
```
I also exported the results: s3://redwood-ci/results/2140123456/tinyq_sum.json
maya: Quick note — infra logs show a bunch of KV cache cold misses during the runs around step ~40 which could explain divergence. Suggest trying kv warmup or increasing prefix cache retention.
eli: Good call. I'll rerun with kv warmup and a different quant profile: ```
python eval.py --model llama3-tinyq --promptset summarization_v2 --split dev --batch 8 --quant-profile q8_0 --kv-warmup True --save debug/warmup_run.json
```
sam: Also, small QA: is the prompt tweak just changing the instruction wrapper or are we altering the system message? If it's the instruction wrapper we should gate on rouge/qa-fluency not just throughput.
rachel: It's the instruction wrapper (extra clarifying sentence). Changed to reduce ambiguity but apparently nudged hallucinations. I think revert for now, then run A/B with fallback to smallq variant as a safety net.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: model-serving:v1.2.3 deployed to staging in 3m 12s — all checks passed.
maya: FYI I added an eval job to the queue with kv warmup + q8 profile, id job-2140125. Will post results when done.
sam: Reviewing PR now, leaving comments about adding a regression test that covers the top 20 failure prompts.
eli: If anyone's blocked on approvals for rollout, ping me. I can approve if the local rerun matches.
rachel: Thanks everyone, plan for today: (1) merge revert PR if no objections, (2) run A/B with fallback + longer kv warmup window, (3) add regression test to the promptset. I’ll follow up with results here. :thumbsup:
